'''Ruth Silverman''' (born 1936 or 1937, died April 25, 2011){{r|wapo}} was an American mathematician and computer scientist known for her research in [[computational geometry]]. She was one of the original founders of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in 1971.{{r|awm|change}}

==Education and career==
Silverman completed a Ph.D. in 1970 at the [[University of Washington]].{{r|diss}}
She was a faculty member at the [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]],
an associate professor at [[Southern Connecticut State University|Southern Connecticut State College]],{{r|scsc}} a computer science instructor at the [[University of the District of Columbia]], and a researcher in the Center for Automation Research at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].{{r|wapo}}

==Contributions==
Silverman's dissertation, ''Decomposition of plane convex sets'',{{r|diss}} concerned the characterization of [[compact set|compact]] [[convex set]]s in the [[Euclidean plane]] that cannot be formed as [[Minkowski sum]]s of simpler sets.{{r|schneider}}

She became known for her research in [[computational geometry]] and particular for highly cited publications on [[k-means clustering]]{{ran|KM}} and [[nearest neighbor search]].{{ran|NN}} Other topics in Silverman's research include [[robust statistics]]{{ran|LT}} and small sets of points that meet every line in finite [[projective plane]]s.{{ran|IP}}
